name: Heian period
summary: Court culture is a major visual/literary anchor; later images often idealize Heian figures, so strict work must distinguish contemporary evidence from later retrospective convention.

wardrobe.text: multilayered court clothing with elaborate color/pattern relationships for elite women

hairstyle_headwear.text: long flowing hair as a strong convention for Heian court women

makeup_grooming.text: specific cosmetic conventions are often known through textual/later depictions; mark them interpretive unless tightly sourced

interior_furniture.text: screened court interiors, mats and low writing/reading arrangements

writing_calligraphy.text: kana literary/calligraphic culture; visible text should be verified

lighting_technology.text: oil lamps / natural daylight appropriate to interior context

visual_arts.text: yamato-e / narrative handscroll context becomes important but varies within/after period

incompatible_or_anachronistic.text: Edo geisha styling as Heian court dress
modern kimono silhouette as direct Heian reconstruction

prompt_fragments.court: Favor layered textile rhythm, long hair, screened interior space and quiet literary action; do not flatten Heian court dress into a modern kimono costume.

sources.supports: long flowing hair and multilayered clothing as Heian court-woman conventions

scope_note: Foundation pack: use as a bounded starting point, not an encyclopedia.
strict_reconstruction_note: Strict mode should distinguish contemporary Heian evidence from later Edo/modern idealizations of Heian court women.
